paraphrase: What Akṣapāda, the foremost of sages, taught as a śāstra for the peace (śama) of the world — on that I shall compose a treatise, a cause of removing the ignorance of bad reasoners.
speaker: Uddyotakara
notes: Wording recalled; confirmed indirectly by Vācaspati's gloss of 'kutārkikājñāna' as the ignorance created by Dignāga and others (local GRETIL e-text of the Tātparyaṭīkā).

paraphrase: Sense-object contact is of six kinds: conjunction, inherence in the conjoined, inherence in what inheres in the conjoined, inherence, inherence in what inheres, and the relation of qualifier and qualified.
speaker: Uddyotakara
notes: Quoted as the Nyāyavārttika's statement in the modern commentary of the local Bhāṣāpariccheda e-text.

paraphrase: Uddyotakara defends the self as distinct from body, senses, mind and cognition against the Buddhist doctrine of no-self, arguing among other things from the unity of the one who recognizes and remembers, and appealing to Buddhist scripture itself as not denying a self.
speaker: Uddyotakara
notes: Chapter-level summary from memory; the appeal to Buddhist scripture (a sūtra on the burden and the bearer of the burden is often cited) needs checking.
